channel.description: Latest news flashes from Israel National News

item.title: Interceptor launched toward false target in southern Lebanon, no sirens sounded
item.description:
A short while ago, an interceptor was launched toward a false target identified in the area in which IDF soldiers are operating in southern Lebanon, the IDF Spokesperson's Unit said.
No sirens were sounded in accordance with protocol.

item.title: Incoming UTJ MK compares yeshiva students' situation to Holocaust era
item.description: Elyakim Shtark compares yeshiva students' fears of arrest at airports to restrictions on crossing borders during the Holocaust.

item.title: Ramming incident in Binyamin: Security officials believe it was not a terror attack
item.description: Following an initial investigation, Israeli security officials believe that the ramming incident near the community of Ateret in the Binyamin region, in which one person was reportedly lightly injured, was not a terrorist attack.

item.description: Draft-eligible individuals who fail to regularize their status must provide IDF clearance within five days of winning a civil service tender or risk losing the job.

item.title: Drama at wedding: Groom’s father collapses, is resuscitated and regains consciousness
item.description: A man in his 60s collapsed at his son’s wedding. Guests performed CPR and delivered three defibrillator shocks before MDA paramedics restored his pulse and he regained consciousness.

item.title: Amb. Danon warns Hezbollah: 'Do not attempt to exploit Israel’s election period'
item.description: Israel’s Ambassador to the UN, Danny Danon, issues a direct warning to Iran and Hezbollah: 'Anyone who dares to attack us will face a devastating response.'

item.title: Report: Israel raised alert level over a possible security threats to elections
item.description:
Israel has raised its level of alert in recent days amid concerns over a possible security escalation, less than two weeks before the elections, Kan News reported.
At this stage, there is no concrete information indicating that Iran or Hezbollah intends to attack, but the IDF is monitoring missile and drone tests being conducted by Iran.
A security official said: “We are acting to ensure that we are not caught by surprise."

item.title: Trump cancels planned livestream of Fort Hood terrorist's execution
item.description: President Donald Trump announces that Nidal Hasan's execution will proceed by firing squad, but will not be broadcast to the public. Victims' immediate families will be permitted to attend.

item.title: Horror in a suitcase: 92 venomous reptiles discovered at German airport
item.description: Customs officers were stunned to find 37 live venomous snakes and 55 lizards hidden in a Mexican passenger’s suitcase, concealed in shampoo bottles, socks and clothing.

item.title: More than 25 years later: Second 9/11 victim identified through new DNA technology
item.description: New York City officials have identified another victim of the September 11 terrorist attacks using advanced genetic genealogy, bringing the total number of identified victims to 1,655.

item.title: IDF and ISA eliminated two Gaza terrorists involved in weapons smuggling
item.description: IDF and ISA eliminated two terrorists who facilitated the smuggling of weapons and military equipment into Gaza.

item.title: B'Tsalmo urges Wiz founder to open McDonald's branches in Judea and Samaria
item.description: B'Tsalmo calls on Assaf Rappaport, who is in advanced talks to acquire the McDonald's Israel franchise, to end the chain's longstanding absence from Judea and Samaria.

item.title: 'I want to hold a Kalashnikov and shoot Jews': IDF reveals letter written by Sinwar's son
item.description: Two years after Yahya Sinwar's elimination, the IDF reveals a letter from his 10-year-old son expressing longing for his father and a desire to shoot Jews.

item.title: Yakir Kososhvili, 35, named as victim of Kiryat Gat Intel plant fire
item.description: Yakir Kososhvili, 35, from Ofakim, was one of those killed in the explosion at the Intel plant in Kiryat Gat. He was pronounced dead yesterday.

item.title: Ayelet Shaked longs for a time when Israeli politics was free of hatred
item.description: Former minister Ayelet Shaked recalls election-season Shabbat visits to synagogues across Israel and expresses hope for a return to respectful debate without toxic polarization.

item.title: Hezbollah admits ownership of Lebanese-seized explosives: 'Bound for Attacks on IDF'
item.description: Hezbollah admits explosives seized in Lebanon belonged to the group, claiming they were intended for attacks on Israeli forces and demanding their return.

item.title: Two killed in Houthi missile attack on Yemeni government headquarters
item.description: Five explosions reported at the presidential palace in Aden. Prime Minister and cabinet ministers unharmed, while two guards were killed and six others injured.

item.title: Rabbi Shmuel Eliyahu: ‘Every vote helps shape the future of Israel’
item.description: Safed Chief Rabbi Shmuel Eliyahu urges the public to vote, warning that “Jewish lives, the Torah of Israel, and the settlement of the Land of Israel" depend on it.

item.title: CENTCOM: USS George H.W. Bush returned to Arabian Sea after break in Thailand
item.description: The United States Central Command (CENTCOM) confirmed Thursday that the USS George H.W. Bush has returned to the Arabian Sea following a visit to Thailand. The aircraft carrier's 5,000 crew members and embarked personnel continue to support CENTCOM operations in the Middle East during a scheduled deployment.

item.title: IDF arrests key terrorist weapons trader in Jenin
item.description:
This morning (Thursday), IDF soldiers completed a special operation in the Jenin area. During the operation, IDF soldiers, guided by the Shin Bet, apprehended a terrorist who was affiliated with the Jenin terror network, which was dismantled during Operation “Iron Wall," an operation aimed at dismantling terrorist networks in Northern Samaria.
The terrorist served as a key weapons trader and, during his involvement with the network, operated to acquire and transfer weapons to the Jenin terror network.

item.title: Watch: A chase in Rahat ends with a surprise for Border Police officers
item.description: During an operation targeting illegal residents in Rahat, Southern District Border Police officers spotted a motorcyclist riding without license plates and after a chase found he was riding a stolen vehicle.

item.title: Netanyahu: I called al-Sharaa, and the Druze massacre stopped
item.description: Netanyahu says he personally called Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa during the 2025 Suwayda massacre and vowed Israel would continue protecting Syria’s Druze.
